'''Jens K. Nørskov''' is the [https://villumfonden.dk/da/group/grantsubarea/villum-kann-rasmussen-professorat Villum Kann Rasmussen professor] at the [[Technical University of Denmark]].<ref>{{cite web|title=DTU Department of Physics: Jens Nørskov |url=https://www.dtu.dk/english/service/phonebook/person?id=1875&tab=1}}</ref> He is a Danish physicist known for his scientific work on [[heterogeneous catalysis]].<ref name="MedfordMosesJacobsenPeterson2022-1">{{Cite journal |last=Medford |first=Andrew J. |last2=Moses |first2=Poul Georg |last3=Jacobsen |first3=Karsten Wedel |last4=Peterson |first4=Andrew A. |date=2022-08-05 |title=A Career in Catalysis: Jens Kehlet Nørskov |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acscatal.2c02217 |journal=ACS Catalysis |volume=12 |issue=15 |pages=9679–9689 |doi=10.1021/acscatal.2c02217 |issn=2155-5435|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Education ==
Jens Nørskov earned his MSc in Physics and Chemistry in 1976<ref name="Autobiography">{{cite journal |last1=Nørskov |first1=Jens K. |title=Short Autobiography of Jens K. Nørskov |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry C |date=16 January 2025 |volume=129 |issue=2 |pages=1027–1028 |doi=10.1021/acs.jpcc.4c08365}}</ref> and his PhD in [[Theoretical Physics]] in 1979 from the [[University of Aarhus]] [[Denmark]] under [https://fy.chalmers.se/~tfybil/ B. I. Lundqvist].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-02 |title=PhD theses |url=https://phys.au.dk/en/research/publications/phd-theses |access-date=2026-11-03 |website=phys.au.dk |publisher=Aarhus University |language=en}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Following his PhD, he served as a research fellow, postdoctoral associate and staff scientist at various institutions including [[IBM T.J. Watson Research Center]], [[Nordic Institute for Theoretical Physics|Nordita]], and [[Haldor Topsøe (company)|Haldor Topsoe]]. In 1987, Jens Nørskov began serving as a research professor at [[Technical University of Denmark]] and was named professor of theoretical physics in 1992. In June 2010, he moved to [[Stanford University]] to become the Leland T. Edwards Professor of Chemical Engineering and the Founding Director of the [https://suncat.stanford.edu SUNCAT Center for Interface Science and Catalysis]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Management {{!}} SUNCAT - Center for Interface Science and Catalysis |url=https://suncat.stanford.edu/about/management |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=suncat.stanford.edu}}</ref> at [[Stanford University|Stanford]] and [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|SLAC]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=People {{!}} SUNCAT - Center for Interface Science and Catalysis |url=https://suncat.stanford.edu/people |access-date=2026-11-03 |website=suncat.stanford.edu}}</ref> In July 2018, he moved back to the Technical University of Denmark to hold the [https://villumfonden.dk/en/group/grantsubarea/villum-kann-rasmussen-professorship Villum Kann Rasmussen Chair].<ref>{{cite web |title=DTU professorship for top researcher from Stanford University |url=https://www.dtu.dk/english/news/2018/01/dtu-professorship-for-top-researcher-from-stanford-university?id=21ed8a03-2f5c-4254-bf29-1061b0c1c43e}}</ref> Nørskov was the chair of the [https://dg.dk/en/ Danish National Research Foundation] 2019-2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Formandsskifte i DG's bestyrelse |date=20 December 2023 |url=https://www.dg.dk/formandsskifte-i-dgs-bestyrelse/}}</ref>

== Research ==
Jens Nørskov has since the mid-1970s made extensive contributions in both theory development and application of theory to a wide range of catalytic systems. He is known for his work on electronic structure theory and the description of surfaces, catalysis, materials, nanostructures, and biomolecules.<ref name="MedfordMosesJacobsenPeterson2022-1" /> He is the central figure in a "school of heterogeneous catalysis" where he together with more than 950 collaborators over the past 50 years has published more than 780 scientific papers.<ref name="MedfordMosesJacobsenPeterson2022-1" /> Jens Nørskov has throughout his career focused on the integration of theory and experiments in the fields of surface science and catalysis, and has together with collaborators developed many key concepts, such as Effective Medium Theory, the Hammer-Nørskov ''d''-band model, the computational hydrogen electrode, scaling relations for adsorption energies/reaction energy barriers, and models for understanding electronic- and spin-effects in alkali and rare-earth promotion of catalytic activity.<ref name="MedfordMosesJacobsenPeterson2022-1" /> His scientific work has established a broad atomic-scale understanding of trends in catalysis over transition metal surfaces and his computational research has in several instances led to the development of new ideas for catalysts e.g. for thermal methanation and ammonia synthesis as well as electrochemical ammonia and fuel-cell catalysis.<ref name="research">{{cite web|title=Nørskov receives the Somorjai Award |url=http://www.dtu.dk/English/About_DTU/News.aspx?guid=%7B78F8B735-7CE6-4744-A882-C279E65BD60E%7D |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120129152812/http://www.dtu.dk/English/About_DTU/News.aspx?guid=%7B78F8B735-7CE6-4744-A882-C279E65BD60E%7D |archive-date=2012-01-29 }}</ref><ref name="RSC">{{cite web|title=Cheaper catalysts designed by Computer|url=http://www.rsc.org/chemistryworld/News/2008/June/05060802.asp}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Hydrogen production|url=http://cosmiclog.nbcnews.com/_news/2011/05/02/6571207-fill-er-up-with-hydrogen|newspaper=MSNBC}}</ref>

== Honours ==
Jens Nørskov is an Elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows archive |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/aps-fellowship |access-date=2026-11-04 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> and a foreign member of the [[National Academy of Engineering|US National Academy of Engineering]],<ref>{{cite web |title=US National Academy of Engineering |url=https://www.nae.edu/MemberDirectory.aspx}}</ref> and is a member of the [[Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Royal Danish Academy of Sciences and Letters |url=http://www.royalacademy.dk/en/Members/Noerskov-Jens-Kehlet}}</ref> the [https://atv.dk/about-atv Danish Academy of Technical Sciences],<ref>{{cite web |title=Akademiet for de Tekniske Videnskaber |url=https://atv.dk/sites/atv.dk/files/media/document/Medlemsliste_ATV_oktober_2018.pdf}}</ref> [[Academia Europaea|Academia Europaea.]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Academia Europaea |url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Acad_Main/List_of_Members}}</ref> He holds honorary doctorates from the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] (TU/e),<ref>{{cite web |title=TU/e honorary doctorate |url=http://www.camd.dtu.dk/English/Events/Latest_news.aspx?guid=%7B5DBBF795-DC59-4879-9CD5-B08836FEE91A%7D |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120330143004/http://www.camd.dtu.dk/English/Events/Latest_news.aspx?guid=%7B5DBBF795-DC59-4879-9CD5-B08836FEE91A%7D |archive-date=2012-03-30 }}</ref> the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]] (NTNU), the [[Technical University of Munich]] (TUM) and from the [[University of Jyväskylä]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ntnu.no/forskning/aeresdoktorer |title=NTNU's overview of honorary doctorates |language=Norwegian |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102200919/http://www.ntnu.no/forskning/aeresdoktorer |url-status=dead |archive-date=2014-01-02 }}</ref>

Jens Kehlet Nørskov is married to Bodil Kehlet Nørskov.
